question: Bowman's layer of the cornea can regenerate after injury, similar to the corneal epithelium.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Bowman's layer does NOT regenerate. Damage results in permanent scar formation. Only the corneal epithelium has regenerative capacity via limbal stem cells.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — Bowman's layer CANNOT regenerate. Once damaged, it is permanently replaced by fibrous scar tissue (leucoma). This is in sharp contrast to the corneal epithelium, which regenerates completely within 48–72 hours.
